item.title: Oyebanji seeks FG support for livestock development
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, has sought increased Federal Government support and collaboration to expand livestock development, create jobs and boost economic opportunities in the state. Oyebanji made the appeal on Tuesday while receiving the Minister of Livestock Development, Idi Mukhtar Maiha, who was in the state to commission an ultra-modern veterinary hospital in Ado-Ekiti and inspect ongoing projects under the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (LPRESS) programme. The governor said livestock development had enormous potential to improve agricultural productivity, generate wealth, create employment and strengthen livelihoods. He called for stronger collaboration between the state and the Federal Government to harness opportunities in the sector, particularly through interventions aimed at improving livestock production and developing its value chain. Oyebanji commended President Bola Tinubu for establishing a separate Ministry of Livestock Development, describing agriculture and livestock as critical sectors for job creation and economic growth. He said his administration was committed to working with the Federal Government, investors and other stakeholders to unlock the sector’s potential and position Ekiti as an attractive destination for livestock investment. The governor urged the minister to assess the state’s ongoing projects, particularly the Ikun Dairy Farm, where he said federal intervention was needed to expand operations and improve sustainability. “I don’t believe in noise making; I believe the only way to advertise yourself is by showcasing your achievements,” he said. He added that the state had reached a stage where additional Federal Government support was necessary to enable its livestock initiatives to achieve greater impact. Earlier, Maiha commended Oyebanji for prioritising agriculture as a means of tackling poverty and unemployment, creating wealth and expanding economic opportunities. The minister assured the governor of the Federal Government’s readiness to strengthen its partnership with Ekiti to expand the agricultural value chain, increase production and sustain the state’s efforts towards food security. Maiha said his working visit included the commissioning of the veterinary hospital and inspection of LPRESS projects across the state. The facilities scheduled for inspection included the Ikun Dairy Farm, Emure Poultry Hub, cattle market in Ado-Ekiti, the ongoing construction of a semi-automated abattoir and the Erifun Broiler Processing Plant in Ado-Ekiti, among others. Also present at the meeting were the Chief of Staff, Niyi Adebayo; Special Adviser on Agriculture and Food Security, Ebenezer Boluwade; Special Adviser on Media, Yinka Oyebode; and LPRESS State Coordinator, Olayinka Adedipe. item.title: Ilhan Omar wins fifth US Congress term despite Trump attacks
item.description: Democratic Congresswoman Ilhan Omar has won a fifth term in the United States House of Representatives, retaining her seat for Minnesota’s 5th Congressional District despite criticism from President Donald Trump and an ongoing federal investigation. Omar defeated Republican candidate John Nagel in Tuesday’s midterm elections, according to projections by CBS News. The Somali-born lawmaker has been a vocal critic of Trump and has repeatedly faced attacks from the president over her background and political views. Her re-election comes amid a federal investigation involving allegations concerning her immigration and naturalisation records. On October 12, federal agents searched Omar’s Washington, DC, residence as part of the investigation. Her phone and passport were reportedly seized, while subpoenas were issued to some of her relatives. Trump had called on the congresswoman to resign, renewing allegations of identity fraud after a court filing identified her by an additional name. Omar has consistently denied any wrongdoing and has not been charged with a crime. Former US President Barack Obama has accused Trump of targeting the Minnesota lawmaker because of her political views. Omar has represented Minnesota’s 5th Congressional District since 2019, after winning the 2018 midterm elections. She was among the first two Muslim women elected to the US House of Representatives. In her victory speech, Omar said her re-election demonstrated that voters would support candidates who prioritised compassion and empathy in their leadership. item.title: Plateau PDP Chieftain Zang rejects APC campaign council appointment
item.description: …Reaffirms loyalty to party By Golok Nanmwa, Jos A chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Plateau State, Hon. Aminu Zang, has rejected his inclusion in the All Progressives Congress (APC) 2027 Presidential and Governorship Campaign Council in the state, insisting that he remains a committed member of the opposition party. Zang, whose name reportedly appeared as number 254 on the published list of the APC Campaign Council’s Central Planning Committee, said he was neither consulted nor informed before his name was included in the committee. In a statement titled “Clarification on My Inclusion in the 2027 Plateau State Presidential and Governorship Campaign Council – Central Planning Committee (CPC)”, Zang said his political allegiance remained firmly with the PDP and the Rainbow Coalition. He said, “While I sincerely appreciate those who considered me worthy of inclusion and deemed me suitable for the responsibilities associated with this important assignment, I wish to state, unequivocally and without any ambiguity, that I remain an unrepentant and committed member of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) of the RAINBOW COALITION extraction.” Speaking in a telephone conversation with our correspondent, Zang said, “They didn’t consult me. I’m not angry, so to speak. “But, like, if you read the statement that I issued, I thanked those who felt that I was worthy of inclusion in the campaign council list.” He added, “Unfortunately for them, I am a bona fide member of the PDP, so I cannot belong to the PDP and now be in the APC campaign council team. I cannot.” On his political position ahead of the 2027 general elections, Zang said, “I am supporting Wike’s position that Tinubu returns, but for the governor, no way. I’m in the PDP.” He further declared, “Of course, we have a candidate in the PDP, Chief Kefas Wungak Ropshik.” He also disclosed that the PDP had yet to constitute its campaign council, saying, “No, not yet. They are working on it.” In his statement, Zang urged political stakeholders, party members, supporters and members of the public to embrace peace, tolerance, civility and political decorum ahead of the 2027 general elections. He said, “The electoral process should be approached with maturity, mutual respect and a strong sense of responsibility.” He also urged all stakeholders to seek the guidance and intervention of Almighty God for a peaceful electoral process. item.title: Trump rout a ‘new era’, could reset ties – S/Africa president
item.description: President Cyril Ramaphosa said Wednesday the Democrats’ rout of the Republicans in US midterm elections heralded a “new era in world relations” and could thaw strained ties between Pretoria and Washington. US-South Africa tensions have mounted over a range of policy disputes, culminating in Washington’s removal this week of South Africa from a trade deal offering eligible sub-Saharan African countries preferential US market access. “I do think that this group is going to introduce a new era in world relations,” Ramaphosa told reporters when asked about the Democratic result. “We’re hoping that on a bilateral basis, there will be a coming together of minds where we will find a proper path forward on geopolitics as well as on trade matters and investment matters,” Ramaphosa said, speaking after voting in local government elections. The US decision to exclude South Africa as well as Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) is set to take effect on January 1, with fears it could cost the battered local economy thousands of jobs. South Africa is the biggest beneficiary of the programme. The two countries have clashed over race, trade and diplomacy, with Washington cutting aid, imposing tariffs, expelling South Africa’s ambassador and boycotting a G20 summit in Johannesburg, against the backdrop of the country’s unresolved legacy of white minority rule. Last year, President Donald Trump berated Ramaphosa in the Oval Office over discredited claims of a “white genocide”. South Africa — Africa’s most industrialised nation — is the United States’ largest trading partner on the African continent, with more than 500 US businesses and 30,000 US citizens based in the country. item.title: ‘We will inflict further defeats on Trump’ – Iran’s Judiciary Chief
item.description: Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei said Wednesday that anyone expecting a shift in US policy was “seriously mistaken”, hours after midterm elections dealt a blow to President Donald Trump. “Those who still harbour even the slightest hope that the behaviour of the hegemonic system might change through partisan or factional shifts, or who imagine that making concessions to the United States can dissuade it from hostility towards the Iranian nation, are seriously mistaken,” Khamenei said in a written statement published on his website. Democrats seized control of the US Congress in Tuesday’s midterms, reflecting anger over living costs, tariffs and the US war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring. Khamenei’s remarks come with diplomatic efforts underway to avert renewed fighting in the war, which broke out on February 28. US and Israeli leaders have in recent days threatened to resume attacks against Iran. “Should such aggressions be repeated, the war’s scope will become much wider,” said Khamenei, who has yet to appear in public since he took power in March. Earlier, Iran’s chief negotiator in talks with the US, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said Americans had voted against war. “Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message,” he posted on X. “If the US govt betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare,” Ghalibaf said. Iran’s judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei also hailed the election results, saying Trump had been “defeated both militarily and politically”. “We will certainly inflict further defeats on him,” he added. Khamenei, 57, was named supreme leader after US-Israeli strikes at the start of the war killed his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. The new leader has since communicated through written messages. item.title: ‘I’ll leave my wife if she becomes president and governs like Tinubu’ — Amaechi
item.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) vice-presidential candidate, Rotimi Amaechi, has said he would leave his wife if she became president and governed like President Bola Tinubu. Amaechi stated this during an interview with Rapid TV, urging Nigerians to put aside religious, political and ethnic affiliations and reject Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election. The former Rivers State governor said his emotional attachment to his wife would not prevent him from opposing her if her administration performed like Tinubu’s. “Today, the closest person in my life is my wife, not my children. So tomorrow, if my wife becomes president and is doing what Tinubu is doing, I’ll be mad to follow my wife, despite my emotional attachment to her. It’s either she changes, or I leave her,” he said. Amaechi urged Nigerians to assess the President’s performance rather than allow personal affiliations to influence their political choices. “I expect Nigerians not to… forget religion, forget politics, forget ethnicity. Just abandon Tinubu,” he said. The ADC candidate argued that Nigerians had already experienced Tinubu’s leadership and should consider giving the opposition a chance in 2027. “There’s a difference between Tinubu’s team and our team. They have been tested, so you know that the next four years you will die. We have not been tested, so give us a chance,” he said. Amaechi, however, acknowledged that he had previously held public office as governor and minister, saying his performance in those positions could be assessed by Nigerians. “The only person you can say that has been tested is me, because I’ve been a governor. But my record speaks for itself. I was once a minister. Projects are out there,” he said. He urged Nigerians to assess his record in Rivers State, adding that his performance as governor was open to public scrutiny. “I was once a governor. Rivers State is there, anybody can go and verify. You can do your referendum,” Amaechi said. He maintained that neither he nor ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, had been tested at the national level as president and vice-president. item.title: FG warns landlords renting properties to terrorists; collaborators face 20-year jail term
item.description: The Federal Government has warned landlords who rent out their properties to terrorists, as well as individuals who host preparatory meetings with terrorist groups, that they risk prosecution under the Terrorism Prevention and Prohibition Act, 2022. Mijinyawa Zakari, a director in the Legal Office of the National Security Adviser (NSA), gave the warning on Tuesday in Abuja during a press briefing on the recently concluded 11th phase of the trial of terrorism suspects. Zakari said the law criminalised several activities associated with terrorism, including preparatory offences and providing material or financial support to terrorist groups. He explained that providing support to terrorism attracted a minimum prison sentence of 20 years, while knowingly renting properties to terrorists was also a prosecutable offence. “A careful reading of the Terrorism Prevention and Prohibition Act, 2022, will indicate that Sections 11 to 33 provide for a wide range of offences, including preparatory offences,” he said. According to him, the government’s strategy is to strengthen its response to terrorism by targeting not only direct perpetrators but also individuals and organisations that facilitate their activities. “The strategy is to ensure that there is dominance across all fields. When you talk about collaborators, you deal with what the investigation has revealed. “For example, providing support to terrorism attracts a minimum sentence of 20 years. Renting your property to a terrorist is also an offence. “You may not have a clear-cut act of terrorism or a harmful act, but all those actions, including holding a preparatory meeting with a terrorist group, constitute offences,” he said. Zakari urged Nigerians, particularly journalists and other stakeholders, to familiarise themselves with the provisions of the law to understand the range of activities classified as terrorism-related offences. He also warned companies against receiving funds linked to terrorism, saying they could face severe sanctions regardless of whether the money was eventually used to commit a terrorist offence. He said a company found guilty of receiving terrorist financing could be fined N200 million, while its principal officers could face prosecution and the company itself could be wound up. “That is why there is a need for increased awareness of what constitutes a terrorist offence in Nigeria. Reading those sections will really help us,” he said. He encouraged journalists and other stakeholders to obtain copies of the Act and study its relevant provisions to better understand the government’s counter-terrorism strategy. Zakari added that the government was strengthening its investigative capacity to ensure that more individuals and organisations involved in terrorism financing and other forms of support were brought to justice. item.title: Pastor, three others killed as gunmen attack Benue community
item.description: … as two-hour incursion left eight injured, traders fleeing for safety By Peter Duru, Makurdi At least four persons, including a man said to be a pastor, have been killed, while eight others sustained varying degrees of injuries following an attack by suspected armed herdsmen on Abeda Shitile community in Gaambe-Tiev, Logo Local Government Area (LGA), of Benue State. The attack reportedly occurred on Tuesday, at about 5pm during the community’s market day, when traders and residents were preparing to return to their homes. A community leader, who spoke on condition of anonymity, disclosed that the attackers stormed the area and opened fire on unsuspecting residents, triggering panic and confusion. According to him, the gunmen operated for more than two hours, leaving residents scampering for safety as sporadic gunshots echoed across the community. “The attack was suspected to be carried out by armed herders and started around 5pm when traders and other residents were preparing to leave the market. Suddenly, we heard heavy gunshots, and people began running in different directions to escape,” the community leader said. He explained that the attackers reportedly began their operation around a POS shop owned by one Ernest Atindi Tor, located in the Ikyô Tor Dukur area, before extending their assault towards the motor park along Afia Road. “It was a terrifying experience for the people. The gunmen moved from one location to another, shooting indiscriminately. The attack lasted for over two hours, and several people were caught up in the incident. “Four persons were confirmed dead in the attack. They were identified as Msoo Chan, Pastor Terungwa Tyonungo, Suurshater Iornumbe and Dodo Shingir,” he added. He disclosed that their remains have been recovered and deposited at a mortuary in the area. According to him, “eight other persons who sustained injuries during the incident were identified as Kumater Awua, Miracle Gangera, Tsetim Terungwa, Iortyom Helen, Seember Aondongu, Kofi Aondosoo, Chuku Okoro and Orker Iortyom. “The injured victims are currently receiving medical attention at a health facility in the area,” he said. Efforts to reach the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, were unsuccessful at the time of this report. item.title: 2027: APC cannot find evidence against Obi – Utomi
item.description: Prof. Pat Utomi has said the inability of the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led Federal Government to prosecute the presidential candidate, of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, over alleged wrongdoing reflects the absence of credible evidence against him. Utomi made the assertion in a post on his X platform on Wednesday, arguing that if Obi had engaged in corruption or had any incriminating issues, the government would have used them to move against him, particularly as an opposition figure. He alleged that the political establishment was uncomfortable with Obi because it could not find credible wrongdoing to use against him. “I’ve said this many times, if Peter Obi had any skeletons in his cupboard or was corrupt like many other politicians, this APC-led administration would have seized the opportunity to arrest him, lock him up and keep him behind bars until after the election, especially as an opposition figure,” Utomi wrote. He added that the inability to find what he described as damaging information against Obi had made the former Anambra State governor a threat to the political establishment. The political economist also questioned what he described as a contradiction in the attitude of Nigerians who, according to him, reject Obi despite his willingness to be investigated by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), while embracing politicians he accused of betraying the public trust. “What strange contradiction has taken hold of some of our consciences? You reject a man who openly challenges the EFCC to prove that he is corrupt (which he is not), yet readily and openly embrace those who have stolen your future,” he said. Utomi further criticised what he described as public acceptance of political leadership associated with corruption, questioning why some Nigerians appeared comfortable with conditions that had contributed to their suffering. He urged Nigerians to reflect on their attitude towards integrity and accountability in public office. The comments come amid continuing political debates over Obi’s record in public service, accountability and the conduct of political leaders ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Spain’s transport minister resigns after train crash kills 69
item.description: Spain’s Transport Minister, Oscar Puente, has resigned less than a week after a deadly train collision that killed 69 people, making it the second major railway disaster in the country in less than a year. Puente also withdrew from the upcoming general election, saying he had initially decided to step down immediately after last week’s accident but remained in office to coordinate the government’s initial response. “A transport minister in a country like Spain cannot continue in office with two accidents of this severity in less than a year,” Puente said, referring to the latest collision and a high-speed train derailment in Andalusia in January, which claimed 46 lives. The latest accident occurred last Wednesday when a high-speed train operated by state-owned Renfe crashed into a stationary train on the Madrid-Seville line in central Spain’s Castilla-La Mancha region. The collision reportedly happened at an estimated speed of between 100 and 125 miles per hour, after the Renfe train slammed into a privately operated Iryo train. Reports indicated that trains on a section of the route had been ordered to stop following a signal failure. However, central controllers in Madrid, who had assumed control after the failure, authorised the Renfe train to continue its journey, resulting in the collision. Following the accident, services on the Madrid-Seville route have been reduced as the Railway Safety Agency reviews the line’s safety systems. The government is also working to complete the delayed deployment of the European Rail Traffic Management System, which is designed to improve railway safety and coordination. Additional measures under consideration include an artificial intelligence system designed to reduce human error by detecting anomalies and monitoring conversations between train drivers and railway controllers. Puente said Spain would become the first country to introduce such a safety mechanism. Meanwhile, victims of the latest accident and their families are expected to receive compensation under a 30-million-euro ($33.5 million) assistance package announced by Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez. Bereaved families will receive 72,121 euros ($80,776) in direct assistance, alongside an equal amount in advance compensation. The latest disaster has renewed concerns about railway safety in Spain, particularly following two major train accidents within a period of less than a year. item.title: Mane, Hakimi, Amad make CAF Men’s Player of the Year shortlist [Full List]
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Senegal forward Sadio Mane, Morocco defender Achraf Hakimi and Ivory Coast winger Amad Diallo have been named among the 10 nominees for the 2026 Confederation of African Football Men’s Player of the Year award. The nominees were announced by CAF on Wednesday, with the trio joined by seven other players in the race for the continent’s top individual football honour. The full list comprises Amad Diallo (Ivory Coast), Yoane Wissa (DR Congo), Antoine Semenyo (Ghana), Ismael Saibari, Achraf Hakimi, Brahim Diaz (Morocco), Ismaila Sarr, Pape Gueye, Sadio Mane (Senegal) and Teboho Mokoena (South Africa). Other categories announced include the Men’s Young Player of the Year, Men’s National Team of the Year, Men’s Club of the Year and Men’s Coach of the Year. The 10 nominees for the Young Player of the Year award are Ibrahim Maza, Christian Kofane, Christ Inao, Yan Diomande, Hamza Abdelkarim, Caleb Yirenkyi, Ismaël Kamissoko, Abdellah Ouazane, Ayoub Bouaddi and Ibrahim Mbaye. The 10 nominees for the Men’s Goalkeeper of the Year award are Oussama Benbot (Algeria), Vozinha (Cabo Verde), Yahia Fofana (Ivory Coast), Lionel Mpasi (DR Congo), El Mahdy Soliman, Mostafa Shobeir (Egypt), Ahmed Reda Tagnaouti, Yassine Bounou (Morocco), Édouard Mendy (Senegal) and Ronwen Williams (South Africa). For the Men’s National Team of the Year, Algeria, Cabo Verde, Côte d’Ivoire, DR Congo, Egypt, Ghana, Morocco, Senegal, South Africa and Tunisia made the shortlist. The Club of the Year category features CR Belouizdad, USM Alger, AS Maniema Union, Zamalek SC, AS FAR, Olympic Club Safi, RS Berkane, Mamelodi Sundowns, Al Hilal SC and ES Tunis. Meanwhile, Lamine N’Diaye, Pedro Leitão Brito, popularly known as Bubista, Sébastien Desabre, Hossam Hassan, Moatamed Gamal, Alexandre Santos, Mohamed Ouahbi, Walid Regragui, Pape Thiaw and Miguel Cardoso are nominated for the Men’s Coach of the Year award. The 2026 CAF Awards ceremony is scheduled to take place in Lagos on Monday, December 7. item.title: Palace’s Mateta banned for three games after red card appeal fails
item.description: Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta will serve a three-match ban after officials rejected an appeal against his red card in Saturday’s 2-0 Premier League defeat at Tottenham. The France international, 29, was sent off in the 13th minute at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium after a late challenge on Spurs captain Micky van de Ven. Mateta was originally shown a yellow card by referee Michael Oliver, but it was upgraded to red following a VAR review. He will be suspended for Palace’s league match at home to Liverpool on Sunday, in addition to fixtures against Coventry and Hull later this month. A statement from the Football Association said: “An independent regulatory commission has dismissed claims of both wrongful dismissal and excessive punishment in relation to Jean-Philippe Mateta.” The post Palace’s Mateta banned for three games after red card appeal fails appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Police avert Obi-Kwankwaso, APC supporters clash in Calabar
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu CALABAR Police and other security operatives on Wednesday prevented a possible violent clash in Calabar, Cross River State, between hundreds of supporters of Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso and a large group of All Progressives Congress (APC) supporters on a campaign walk. The meeting, organised by the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, was to feature Obi, its presidential candidate, and Kwankwaso, his running mate. It was scheduled to be held at a hotel along Murtala Mohammed Highway, near the U.J. Esuene Stadium. The APC supporters, who had mobilised in large numbers for a street rally in the same area, included members of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria, ALGON, and other party faithful. Tension rose as both groups met in front of the hotel. Hundreds of Obi and Kwankwaso supporters had gathered there, partially blocking the highway in an apparent attempt to stop the APC supporters from reaching the venue. Security operatives separated the two groups and diverted the APC crowd. The hotel management later restricted access to its premises as security personnel maintained order around the facility. A police officer, who declined to be named, said the intervention was necessary to forestall bloodshed. “What we have done is very necessary; otherwise, it would have been a bloody scene,” he said. Confirming the incident to Vanguard in a WhatsApp message, the Cross River State Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Sunday Eitokpah, said the command acted to avert a breakdown of law and order. He stated, “Cross River State Police Command, through timely intervention and constructive engagement, helped avert a possible confrontation between participants at a presidential town hall meeting organised by the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) at Hotel along the Murtala Mohammed Highway in Calabar and a group of supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) undertaking a rally/road walk towards the Governor’s Office. “Upon the convergence of both groups in front of the Metropolitan Hotel, police officers promptly engaged them, appealing to all parties to exercise restraint, maintain peace and ensure that their respective activities were conducted peacefully and in accordance with the law.” Officials of both political camps had not commented on the incident as of the time of filing this report, although some senior APC officials were seen leaving the vicinity of the NDC meeting. Obi and Kwankwaso had not also arrived at the venue as of the time of this report, while party stalwarts and supporters thronged the hotel premises and its frontage. item.title: Slavery reparations ‘not feasible’ for UK – Foreign minister
item.description: Britain’s Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has said it was “not feasible” for the country to pay reparations for slavery, after King Charles III expressed remorse amid calls for a formal apology and compensation. “It’s not the right answer. It’s not practical. It’s not feasible for us, but there are things we can work on co-operatively,” Miliband told the BBC in an interview aired Wednesday. He added that London would not “shift our position on reparations”. Miliband also hinted that Britain could issue a long-demanded formal apology for its role in the slave trade next year when it hosts a G20 leaders’ summit. Asked whether the UK could reach that point by the meeting in Manchester next November, Miliband said: “Broadly speaking, yes”. But he insisted an apology would not pave the way for financial compensation. At the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda, Prime Minister Andy Burnham floated a “debt reset” plan for the poorest Commonwealth countries that could alter interest rates on repayments. Burnham told reporters on Tuesday: “I’ve been very clear that we do not support reparations … but it’s not the case that we don’t support countries in the Commonwealth around development helping them with debt issues that they’ve got”. Britain’s pivotal role in slavery has long strained relations with its former colonies. Burnham said he would have “difficult conversations” to safeguard the Commonwealth’s future. In a tense Commonwealth meeting in Samoa in 2024, countries backed talks over reparatory justice after Britain, then under Keir Starmer’s leadership, tried to avoid addressing the issue. Burnham’s change of tack has not gone down well at home, with opposition Conservative party leader Kemi Badenoch and the right-wing press criticising his approach. King Charles went further than previous royals when he expressed his “horror”, but stopped short of apologising and stressed Britain’s role in eventually abolishing slavery. The king opened the summit — part of a nine-day Caribbean tour — calling slavery a “monstrous injustice” that “still casts a shadow over these islands and other members” of the 56-nation group of mostly former British colonies. Charles and Queen Camilla are to end their Caribbean tour and depart from Antigua and Barbuda on Wednesday. item.title: 4,000 Newly Employed Public Servants To Strengthen A’Ibom Civil Service, Says Gov Eno
item.description: Akwa Ibom State Governor, Pastor Umo Eno, has said the recruitment of 4,000 new civil servants was aimed at filling identified vacancies and strengthening the state’s public service for improved efficiency and service delivery. Governor Eno spoke on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, during an orientation programme for the newly recruited workers at the Ibom Tropicana Event Centre, Uyo. The orientation follows his earlier announcement directing the newly employed civil servants to resume work on October 1, 2026. Explaining the rationale behind the recruitment, Eno said a staff verification exercise conducted after he assumed office revealed more than 2,000 ghost workers, as well as several employees who had retired but remained on the payroll. He explained that after addressing the identified irregularities, the government found it necessary to fill the resulting vacancies and strengthen the workforce. According to him, the recruitment was not intended to inflate the size of the civil service but to address manpower shortages and improve its capacity to deliver public services. “There was a huge vacancy gap in the Service, so we are not recruiting to bloat the service but to strengthen and make the public service more efficient for excellent work output,” the Governor said. A cross-section of the newly employed civil servants on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. He charged the new employees to demonstrate commitment, discipline, and professionalism in their duties, urging them to bring fresh ideas and innovation into the system. Governor Eno further reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to the prompt payment of salaries and gratuities. Earlier, the Head of the Civil Service, Mrs. Elsie Peters, expressed confidence in the quality of the newly recruited workforce, describing the orientation and training as important steps towards revitalising the state civil service. She acknowledged Governor Eno’s support for the public service and expressed optimism that the new employees would contribute to improved performance and greater efficiency across government institutions. Some of the newly recruited civil servants expressed excitement over their appointments, describing the opportunity to join the state workforce as a significant milestone. They also commended the recruitment process, which they described as fair and credible, saying their selection was based on merit and not favouritism. Among the beneficiaries who shared their experiences were Jennifer Ekott, Glory Wilson and Imo Obot, who expressed appreciation for the opportunity to serve the state. The orientation programme is expected to familiarise the new employees with the values, expectations and responsibilities of the public service as they begin their careers in the Akwa Ibom State Civil Service.
